question: In which year was the National Commission for Women established in India?
solution:
The correct answer is** __1992.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​The** National Commission for Women** was established with the goal of establishing for Indian women an equitable and just standard of living through** judicial and constitutional changes.**
 
• On** January 31, 1992, the first commission** was established, with **Jayanti Patnaik serving as chair**. The National Commission for **Women's first male member is IAS Alok Rawat** (NCW). His selection filled the fourth spot on the body's five members.
 
• The National Commission for Women's Chairperson at the moment is** Ms. Rekha Sharma**. In September 2018, she succeeded** Lalitha Kumaramangalam as the new Chairperson. **​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​The** Commission must have at least six members**, including the chairperson, member secretary, and the remaining five members.

 The chairperson should be chosen by the **national government.**
 
• Member secretaries are also chosen by the** central government**. He or she should be a member of the organisation, a member organisation, or** a management specialist.**
 
• Members of the NCW participate in the planning of **women's socioeconomic development**, suggest policies to promote women's representation in** all fields, and assess women's growth. ​​**
